solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Servant concealed bags with mother

indicators.note: to bag something is to pocket or hold it, so the hiding word wraps around what follows

parts.note: past tense of hide
'with' as in 'and also'
familiar word for one's mother

explanation.surface: A servant has hidden some bags, and her mother is in on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like luggage but is a verb meaning grabs or holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaid is a female servant or personal attendant, an old-fashioned word for a maid.

clue.text: Mountain plants too short to include connifer

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so one word goes inside the other
a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: too means also, in addition
a pine is a typical conifer (the source misspells the word)

explanation.surface: Some mountain plants are too stunted to fit a conifer among them.
explanation.walkthrough: ALSO loses its last letter to ALS, which then holds PINE: AL(PINE)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpines are small plants that grow naturally high on mountains above the tree line, popular in rock gardens.

clue.text: One minister comes in to see governors

indicators.note: something that comes in enters, so these words are placed inside another

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to date them
the Roman numeral for one
a rector is a parish clergyman, a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A government minister arrives to meet the people who run things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks political but is a clergyman here, and 'see' means go out with.
explanation.definitionFit: A directorate is a board of directors, the body that governs and manages an organisation collectively.

clue.text: Massacre after all those in Mexico have left

parts.note: à la means in the style of, as a painting 'after' Rubens

indicators.note: this phrase picks out every interior letter of the word that follows
those inner letters depart, so only the two ends stay behind

parts.note: only the first and last letters of the country remain

explanation.surface: A massacre takes place once all the people in Mexico have gone away.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo, a mission in Texas, then part of Mexico, was where Santa Anna's army killed its defenders in 1836, so the surface is close to history.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo is remembered for the 1836 slaughter of its Texan defenders by the Mexican army; the name stands for that event.

clue.text: Least interesting airport opening for travellers

parts.note: Dulles is the international airport serving Washington DC

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An airport has opened that travellers find utterly boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Dullest is the superlative of dull, so it describes whatever is most boring of all.

clue.text: Cows stand up, quietly going round the bend

indicators.note: round the bend means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
in music p (piano) means quietly, so that letter goes away

parts.note: taken as written
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Cattle stand up and wander silently round a corner in the lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cows' looks like the animals but is a verb. Take P out of STANDUP and rearrange STANDU.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them into submission, and daunts likewise means discourages or intimidates.

clue.text: Bill in nightclub one way to create conflict

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub for dancing
AC is short for account, a bill
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A bill run up in a nightclub is one way to start an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Disaccord is disagreement or lack of harmony, a state of conflict between parties.

clue.text: Advantage of American English

parts.note: abbreviation for the United States
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A question about what benefit American English offers.
explanation.definitionFit: Use means benefit or profit, as in 'what is the use of it?', the same as an advantage.

clue.text: Become upset about artist being alive

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to get angry is to become angry
Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: Someone gets agitated over whether an artist is still living.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a British artist famous for her unmade bed, a regular crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming means swarming or full of life, as in a pond alive with fish.

clue.text: Socket most fit before getting old Walkman?

parts.note: a port is a socket on a computer or device
superlative of able, fit to do something
poetic word for before
standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: The fittest socket is chosen before an old Walkman is plugged in.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a Walkman is one brand of the thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sony Walkman was a famous example of a personal cassette player, a small device carried around for music.

clue.text: A City love story

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article before a vowel
EC is the postcode of the City of London
to dote is to love fondly

explanation.surface: A romantic tale set in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing or interesting tale about a real incident or person.

clue.text: Smoke and ice swirling around one horse

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the mixed letters enclose the next part
swirling things are stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
Roman numeral for one
gee-gee, a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: Smoke and ice swirl around a lone horse on a wintry field.
explanation.walkthrough: GG (gee-gee) is a child's word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciggie is an informal word for a cigarette, and a smoke is slang for the same thing.

clue.text: What makes coffee good? Stirring

parts.note: coffee is brewed from ground beans, the grounds
doing well, faring good

explanation.surface: Asking what makes a good cup of coffee, the answer is stirring it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' seems to answer the coffee question but is a noun: a rising of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundswell is a build-up of public opinion or feeling, a stirring among the people.

clue.text: Mix, when that's so right

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
taken as written
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks when it is all right to mix things.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to sort into groups or to blend different kinds together, giving a mixture.

clue.text: Flog antiquated door

parts.note: to thresh is to beat, as grain is beaten
antiquated means old-fashioned

explanation.surface: An instruction to sell an ancient door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' is British slang for sell, but here it means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the sill or entrance of a doorway, so it stands for the door itself.

clue.text: Downright hard, or having hard shell

indicators.note: the shell holds what goes inside it, the way a case has contents

parts.note: tough means hard; it forms the outer casing
H for hard, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is utterly hard, or else has a hard shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' appears twice and does two jobs: once as a single letter, once with 'shell' as the outer casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough can mean complete or utter, as in 'a thorough nuisance', the same as downright.

clue.text: I'd make good sort of theatre publicist?

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
one who airs something, makes it public

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they would be a good theatre press agent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer itself: a repairer would say 'I make good'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is to mend or put right, which is exactly what a repairer does with broken things.

clue.text: Biannual event short of horses? Bull!

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: equine means relating to horses
an ox is a bull, especially a castrated one

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a twice-yearly event lacking horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull!' looks like an exclamation of disbelief but is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An equinox, when day and night are equal, happens twice a year in March and September.

clue.text: Chicken roll with added duck

indicators.note: something added is slotted into the list, here within it

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, zero

explanation.surface: A chicken roll with duck added, a deli order.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes into ROSTER: RO(O)STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic chicken, the cockerel that crows in the morning.

clue.text: River bed polluted around waste outlet, mostly.

indicators.note: around means encircling the following piece
something polluted is spoiled, so the letters are messed up
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
the anus is the body's outlet for waste

explanation.surface: A riverbed fouled around a sewage pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' could be any river; the scrambled bed letters around the body's outlet pin it down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is Europe's second-longest river, flowing from Germany to the Black Sea.

clue.text: Stretch of thoroughfare with mountain crossing

indicators.note: a mountain crossing a road straddles it, here holding it in the middle

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a road is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A stretch of highway with a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch' looks like a noun for a length of road but is the verb; ben is Scottish for mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden is to widen or extend, the same as to stretch something out.

clue.text: Force to decorate nursing uniform

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, as a mother holds a baby, so one goes inside

parts.note: to dress a window or tree is to decorate it
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is being forced to adorn a nurse's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing' suggests hospitals but signals holding one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion or compulsion by threats, as when someone acts under force.

clue.text: Mistake — primarily, own goal.

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word
a mission is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: An own goal is chiefly a mistake, a football commentator's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Own goal' reads as one football phrase, but the words split to give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is something left out by oversight, which counts as a mistake or error.

clue.text: Useless home record — heading for this

parts.note: being in means being at home
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A useless home recording is headed for this fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or incompetent, lacking skill, so the person is no good at a task.

clue.text: Stop tap being applied to nut.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put an end to a plan
second meaning, read literally: a blow struck on the skull, nut being slang for head

explanation.surface: Stop the tap being fitted to a nut, a plumber's instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tap' and 'nut' suggest plumbing; nut is informal for head, and tap is a light blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something on the head is a British idiom meaning to put a stop to a plan or idea.

clue.text: Reminder of line to be said

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so it is judged on sound

parts.note: a line of people waiting is a queue

explanation.surface: A prompt for an actor's line that must be spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatrical surface fits the answer too: an actor's prompt to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal or prompt that reminds a performer when to come in or speak.

clue.text: Overtake old car made by Kia.

parts.note: ex means former, old
the Kia Cee'd is a family hatchback model

explanation.surface: Overtaking an old Kia on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed is to go beyond or surpass, and overtaking means passing another to go ahead.

clue.text: Very good indication of loose parts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dated British intensifier
second meaning: the clattering noise of something not fixed tight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rattling good' is an old-fashioned British phrase meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a dated intensifier for excellent and the jangling sound heard when components work loose.
